summary: Full backend + frontend regression of One Stock Academy. Created pytest suite (/app/backend/tests) covering health/courses, rule-based chat (23 cases incl. all reported regressions), leads + admin auth/dashboard APIs, and demo enrollment/payment flow: 30/31 assertions passed. Playwright verified home page, chatbot handoff -> lead modal submission, offline/online enroll deep links + demo payment success (OSA-B240753134 paid), admin login (wrong + correct password) with enrollments/leads tables showing the new records, quiz, mentor cards, custom cursor, mobile viewport. Only failure: /api/chat rate limiting is not actually enforced.

minor.issue: Documented 10 msg/min per-IP rate limit never triggers — 15 rapid requests all returned 200 (test_chat_ratelimit.py). Root cause: _chat_rate is keyed on request.client.host, which behind the k8s ingress is the proxy/pod address and is not the real client; key on X-Forwarded-For (first hop) instead. In-memory dict also never evicts old IPs (slow leak).
No brute-force protection / lockout or throttling on the admin password endpoint — unlimited password guesses accepted (only 401s). Single shared password, no per-attempt delay.
Review request refers to POST /api/enroll; actual endpoint is POST /api/orders + POST /api/payments/verify. Docs/credentials note should be aligned (no code bug).

rca_of_the_issue: Chat rate limit: _chat_rate uses request.client.host as the key. Behind the Kubernetes ingress the observed client host is not the end-user IP (and varies), so each request lands in a different/never-saturated bucket; 15 back-to-back /api/chat calls from one machine all returned 200. Fix: derive the client IP from X-Forwarded-For (leftmost entry) with request.client.host as fallback, and periodically drop IP keys older than the window.
